The sprint

Seven days, three controlled steps.

The pilot is intentionally manual. Its job is to show whether a disciplined exception workflow can surface blockers, document commitments and save owner time before anyone buys or builds more software.

01 / TRIAGE

Separate routine overdue work from real disputes.

We review a minimal ageing export, confirm contact and invoice details, and classify each item: ready, missing evidence, promise made, disputed or stop.

02 / PREPARE

Put the next message and owner beside every invoice.

We prepare relationship-safe follow-ups for your approval, identify AP blockers and set a next-check date. You send each approved message from your own business account; we do not contact your customers during the founding pilot.

03 / REPORT

End with a result and an exception map.

You receive the current state, payment promises, unresolved blockers, stopped items and a repeatable weekly routine—not a vanity dashboard.

First-touch draft

Subject: Invoice [ID] — confirming payment status

Hi [approved contact], could you confirm the current status of invoice [ID], due [date]? If anything is blocking processing, please let us know the exact item needed. Thank you.

Every live message is based only on client-supplied facts, approved by the client and sent by the client. Disputes leave the routine workflow immediately.

Scope boundary

Administrative control, not aggressive collection.

The pilot is for undisputed business invoices where preserving the customer relationship matters.

Included

  • Up to 10 overdue B2B invoices
  • Ageing and blocker triage
  • Client-approved reminder drafts
  • Promise-to-pay and exception tracker
  • Seven-day closeout report

Not included

  • Consumer debt or disputed-debt pursuit
  • Legal demands, threats or court action
  • Face-to-face contact
  • Bank access or custody of customer funds
  • A guarantee that any invoice will be paid

Is the pilot worth discussing?

Control and trust

Your authority stays with you.

The validation page collects nothing. If a pilot proceeds, the written scope defines exactly what is shared, who approves each communication and when work stops.

Minimum data

Initial fit needs counts and approximate values only. A scoped pilot uses the minimum invoice metadata required for the agreed queue.

Explicit approval

The client approves the wording, recipient and timing, then sends from its own business account. The founding pilot never contacts the client's customers directly.

Defined stop points

Disputes, hardship, legal escalation, uncertain identity or a request to stop leave the routine workflow immediately.

Evidence sources: Payment Times Regulator, January 2026 · Chaser public pricing · ASIC/ACCC debt-collection conduct guidance.

Privacy and data handling

This page has no analytics, cookies, account creation or server-side form. The fit-check values remain in your browser. If you reply to an invitation, the sender will use your message only to assess and discuss the pilot. A paid pilot will not begin until data fields, access, storage, deletion and approval responsibilities are confirmed in writing.

Founding-pilot terms

The displayed A$249 offer is subject to a written fit and scope confirmation. It covers triage, a maximum of two client-sent message drafts per eligible invoice, response/commitment tracking and a closeout report for up to ten routine, undisputed B2B invoices over seven calendar days. The seven days begin after written acceptance, payment and clean intake. It excludes provider-to-debtor contact, legal advice, consumer debt, disputed-debt pursuit, court action, face-to-face contact, bank access, custody of funds and any guarantee of payment. Either side may decline before the written scope is accepted.
